To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the preservation of tooth structure, ferrule, postless approaches and postless build-up are important factors for the survival of endodontically-treated and restored teeth.

(i) postless approaches have the potential to reduce the risk of catastrophic failure in endodontically-treated posterior teeth; (ii) post type and ferrule effect on the incidence of root fractures are controversial; (iii) the ferrule effect is still relevant in endodontically treated anterior teeth; (iv) the use of adhesive materials in postless approaches is a must.

(i) the ferrule is important to restore ETT, (ii) fiber posts have the potential to increase the risk of root fracture in ETT, (iii) there is no clear evidence that postless restorations are superior in comparison to fiber post restorations, and (iv) the use of postless restoratives should be further investigated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the restoration of ETT with adhesive procedures.
the development of a new approach to the endodontically treated tooth.
the development of new adhesive approaches for the restoration of endodontically-treated posterior teeth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adhesive restoration of ETT is a complex and challenging clinical situation that requires a multidisciplinary approach, with a careful case selection, and an individualized treatment planning.
the current knowledge on the restoration of ETT is still limited and more clinical studies are necessary to better understand the clinical outcomes and the failure modes.
the best option to restore an ETT would be to preserve the tooth structure as much as possible and to avoid a post if possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adhesive dentistry is still evolving and that the future will bring more options for ETT restoration.
the preservation of tooth structure is the key to the survival of the endodontically treated tooth.
the current evidence does not support the use of fiber posts to prevent catastrophic failure of ETT.

adhesive dentistry is still evolving and that the current literature is still contradictory regarding the influence of post types, the role of ferrules and the advantages of postless restorations on the survival of ETT.
